title: Wrap-boundary collision remains open: the content backstop cannot fire, because the colliding state leaves the cursor row blank
description:
Follow-up to CAM-359 (shipped). CAM-359 replaced the content-matching submission oracle with cursor geometry and added `composerLineRetainsPayloadTail` as a backstop for the exact-wrap-boundary residue class. Round-2 review then correctly made that backstop read through a dedicated visible-screen reader. The backstop is nonetheless INERT for the case it exists to close, and the module header at src/tmux/dispatch.ts consequently OVERCLAIMS ('closes that residual gap').

MEASURED EVIDENCE (real claude Ink TUI v2.1.215, tmux pane 80x30, orchestrator probe 2026-07-20, not inferred).

Baseline, empty composer: cursor = (2,26).

Sweep of single-token (character-wrapping) payloads: no length collides. Wrap is LAZY: len=76 leaves the cursor parked at x=78 on the full row; len=77 moves to the continuation row at x=3. The cursor never rests at x=2 with text present, because a character placed on a continuation row puts the cursor at x=3.

  len=74 -> (76,26)   len=76 -> (78,26)   len=77 -> (3,26)   len=153 -> (3,26)

BUT the collision IS reachable when the payload ENDS IN A SPACE that lands on the boundary, because Ink word-wraps the trailing space onto the next row:

  len=75 trailing-space -> (77,26)
  len=76 trailing-space -> (78,26)
  len=77 trailing-space -> (2,26)   <-- IDENTICAL TO THE EMPTY BASELINE
  len=78 trailing-space -> (5,26)

So the collision is real (the round-1 CRITICAL was right), but it occurs ONLY in the trailing-space-at-boundary case.

WHY THE BACKSTOP CANNOT FIRE. In precisely that colliding state the cursor row is BLANK, and the payload tail lives on the row ABOVE:

  row[24] = '----------------------------------------' (composer top border)
  row[25] = '# word word word ... word w'              (payload text + prompt glyph)
  row[26] = ''                                          (cursor rests here, (2,26))
  row[27] = '----------------------------------------' (composer bottom border)

`composerLineRetainsPayloadTail` does `lines[cursorY]` -> '' -> `trimmed.length === 0` -> returns false -> geometry reads unchanged -> verdict DELIVERED. The undelivered payload is silently lost: the original CAM-358 defect, surviving for this residue class. The function's doc comment ('the trailing suffix ... is always CONTIGUOUS on the single row the cursor rests on') is false exactly at the collision. This is structural, not a tuning problem: whenever the geometry collides, the cursor row is whitespace-only BY CONSTRUCTION, so no tail-matching rule keyed on the cursor row can ever detect it.

PROPOSED FIX (exact, not probabilistic). When the geometry pair reads unchanged, discriminate on WHERE THE PROMPT GLYPH IS. An empty composer has the prompt on the cursor row itself; the colliding state has the cursor row blank with the prompt one row up alongside the payload:

  empty:     row[cursorY] = '# Try "how does <filepath> work?"'   (prompt on the cursor row)
  collision: row[cursorY] = ''                                     (blank; prompt at cursorY-1)

So 'the cursor row does not carry the prompt glyph' is a sound, exact 'still composing' signal. It needs no payload-derived matching at all, which also retires MIN_PAYLOAD_TAIL_MATCH and the suffix-length scan (round 2 SUGGESTION: the 2-char floor is loose and a false positive costs a duplicate push). Validate against the real Ink TUI, not the fixture: test/fixtures/dispatch-geometry/raw-echo.ts models wrap behaviour that has already been wrong once (it encoded eager downward wrap until US-R1-001 corrected it).

SCOPE. Replace the tail-matching backstop with the prompt-row discriminator; correct the overclaiming module header and the `composerLineRetainsPayloadTail` doc comment; add a real-tmux regression test driving a TRAILING-SPACE payload at the exact wrap boundary (len 77 at width 80) asserting NOT delivered plus a retry, which is the case no current test covers.

CONSTRAINT (unchanged from CAM-359). Correct in BOTH directions: a delivered payload must not be resent (duplicate sends trip the back-to-back send-keys race, scripts/cam/patterns.md:330) and an undelivered one must not read as delivered.

PRIORITY NOTE. Narrow residue (payload must end in a space AND land exactly on a wrap boundary), and CAM-359 already removed the far larger always-delivered-for-any-wrapped-payload defect. Filed so the gap is tracked rather than silently carried under a comment claiming it is closed.

spec.scope: Replace the inert content backstop in src/tmux/dispatch.ts with a prompt-row discriminator, correct the overclaiming docs, and extend the real-tmux fixture to reproduce the ACTUAL production collision class. (1) Delete composerLineRetainsPayloadTail and MIN_PAYLOAD_TAIL_MATCH; in their place, when geometryUnchanged reads true, resolve the tie on whether the visible-capture row at cursorY carries the prompt glyph anchored at the START of the row. Empty composer: the glyph is on the cursor row -> DELIVERED. Wrap-boundary collision: the cursor row is blank and the glyph sits at cursorY-1 -> NOT delivered, retry. (2) Correct the module header, which currently states composerLineRetainsPayloadTail 'closes that residual gap' (false), and delete the stale doc claim that the payload's trailing suffix 'is always CONTIGUOUS on the single row the cursor rests on' (false exactly at the collision, where that row is blank). State the new narrowing precisely and do NOT claim the gap is fully closed. (3) Extend test/fixtures/dispatch-geometry/raw-echo.ts with a word-wrap mode that reproduces the production collision shape (trailing space wrapped onto the next row, leaving the cursor row BLANK at column 2) and render the production prompt glyph, then add an integration test in test/integration/dispatch-geometry.test.ts driving a trailing-space payload at the exact wrap boundary and asserting NOT delivered plus a retry plus one push-undelivered event. Preserve the round-2 visibleCaptureFn/capturePaneFn separation and the full-pair geometry comparison exactly as they are.
acceptanceCriteria: grep -c 'composerLineRetainsPayloadTail' src/tmux/dispatch.ts returns 0: the function, its export, its call site, and every doc reference are removed.

The module header of src/tmux/dispatch.ts no longer contains the string 'closes that residual gap' and no longer asserts that any trailing suffix is always contiguous on the cursor row; it instead documents the prompt-row discriminator and names the remaining forgery residue (a payload containing a literal prompt glyph landing at a wrap-row start) as NOT closed.

The new discriminator matches the prompt glyph anchored at the START of the cursor row (a start-anchored pattern such as /^\s*[>\u276F]/), NOT the existing IDLE_PROMPT regex /[>\u276F]\s*$/, which is end-anchored and provably does not match the real empty-composer row '\u276F\u00A0Try "how do I log an error?"'.

The discriminator is consulted ONLY on the branch where geometryUnchanged already returned true; the full (cursorX, cursorY) pair comparison in geometryUnchanged is unchanged and is never reduced to a single axis.

A null geometry sample on either side of a send still falls through to retry (fail-closed), and an out-of-range cursorY still yields a safe verdict under noUncheckedIndexedAccess (lines[cursorY] is string | undefined and must be guarded).
The backstop still reads pane content through visibleCaptureFn (visible-screen capture, no -S -), never through capturePaneFn; the round-2 reader separation and its rationale comment survive.

test/fixtures/dispatch-geometry/raw-echo.ts renders the production prompt glyph U+276F followed by U+00A0 in place of the current '> ', and its header documents that the previous char-wrap-only model reproduced a collision shape (cursor row retaining 2 real characters) that does NOT occur in the real Ink TUI.

raw-echo.ts supports a word-wrap mode in which a payload ending in a space that lands exactly on the wrap boundary places the trailing space on the next row, leaving the cursor row BLANK with the cursor at column 2 and the payload plus prompt glyph on the row above.

A new test in test/integration/dispatch-geometry.test.ts drives the real tmux server with a trailing-space payload at the exact wrap boundary in drop mode and asserts the payload is NOT reported delivered: exactly maxAttempts send-keys invocations occur and exactly one push-undelivered event is emitted.

A companion integration test drives the same trailing-space boundary payload in submit mode and asserts exactly one send-keys invocation and zero push-undelivered events, proving the discriminator does not cause a duplicate resend of a delivered payload.

The existing dispatch-geometry integration tests (AC6, AC7, both AC8 cases, the 2*paneWidth generalization) still pass unmodified in behaviour, or any change to them is justified in the commit message as a fixture-model correction rather than a weakened assertion.
bun run typecheck is zero errors, bun test is zero failures, and bun run check:all passes.
gotchas: MEASURED LIVE against a real claude Ink TUI in an 80x30 tmux pane on the current 0.219.0 binary (orchestrator probe 2026-07-20, not inferred). EMPTY composer: cursor (2,26), row[26] = '\u276F\u00A0Try "how do I log an error?"' with the glyph ON the cursor row. COLLISION, 77-char payload ending in a space: cursor (2,26) byte-identical to the empty baseline, row[26] = '' (blank, the cursor row), row[25] = '\u276F\u00A0word word ... w' (payload plus glyph one row up), row[24] and row[27] are the composer borders. This is the exact reproducer; build the fixture to match this shape.

THE FIXTURE CURRENTLY MODELS THE WRONG COLLISION CLASS, for the second time. raw-echo.ts reproduces the residue as char-wrapping where a payload of length k*paneWidth leaves exactly 2 real characters on the trailing row, so the cursor lands at column 2 WITH TEXT PRESENT. That is why MIN_PAYLOAD_TAIL_MATCH = 2 appears to work. The real Ink TUI collision leaves the cursor row BLANK. The fixture header already records that an earlier eager-downward-wrap version made a test pass 'for a reason absent in production'; do not repeat that. Validate the new mode against the measured table above, not against intuition about wrapping.

Wrap is LAZY in the real TUI and single-token payloads NEVER collide: len=76 leaves the cursor at x=78, len=77 moves to x=3, len=153 gives x=3. The cursor never rests at x=2 with text present, because a character on a continuation row puts the cursor at x=3. The collision is reachable ONLY when the payload ends in a space that lands on the boundary. Measured trailing-space sweep: len=75 -> (77,26), len=76 -> (78,26), len=77 -> (2,26) COLLISION, len=78 -> (5,26).

IDLE_PROMPT at src/tmux/dispatch.ts:258 is /[>\u276F]\s*$/ and is END-anchored. It is used by isOrchPaneIdle for the pre-send idle gate and must NOT be reused for this discriminator: the real empty-composer row ends with the placeholder text '?"', not with the glyph, so IDLE_PROMPT does not match it. Introduce a separate start-anchored pattern. Do not modify IDLE_PROMPT or isOrchPaneIdle.

CORRECT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. An undelivered payload must not read as delivered (the CAM-358 silent loss), and a delivered payload must not be resent: duplicate sends trip the back-to-back send-keys race documented at scripts/cam/patterns.md:330. Both directions need a test.

DO NOT OVERCLAIM IN THE DOCS. This discriminator is consulted only when geometry reads unchanged, so a payload that itself contains a literal '>' or '\u276F' landing at the start of a wrap row could still forge an empty-composer reading. That residue is far narrower than the current trailing-space class (which needs only a space) but it is NOT zero. The module header must say so plainly. The header being wrong about exactly this is why CAM-364 exists.

The prompt glyph is U+276F ('\u276F') followed by U+00A0 (non-breaking space), NOT U+003E ('>') and NOT a regular space. Verified by codepoint on the live pane. The fixture's current '> ' is ASCII. Keep the discriminator tolerant of both characters so the fixture and production both match.

capturePaneFn (full scrollback, -S -) and visibleCaptureFn (visible screen, no -S -) diverge in production: src/supervisor/host.ts:1030-1042 passes the supervisor's scrollback closure as capturePaneFn only, and visibleCaptureFn falls back to a fresh visible-screen builder. Indexing a scrollback capture by cursorY reads an arbitrary history line. This was review round 2's fix on CAM-359; preserve it and its rationale comment.

Every sendKeysWhenIdle / sendKeysVerified call site emits the single event kind 'push-undelivered' with detail { paneId, retriesExhausted }. Do not add new event kinds; the four thin-proxy sites (issue.ts, review.ts, spec.ts, orch-recycle-watch.ts) and the sidecar sites all share this contract.

test/integration/dispatch-geometry.test.ts is the ONLY test driving a real tmux server against the geometry oracle; its unit-test siblings structurally cannot catch a defect in the real interaction with tmux cursor tracking. All its tests are test.skipIf(!tmuxAvailable) on a private socket with a pane pinned to 80 columns. New coverage for this residue class belongs there, not in test/dispatch.test.ts.
This story touches src/tmux/dispatch.ts, which the sidecar executes, so the orchestrator must coherence-rebuild after ship. Do not skip it.
domainTerms: submission oracle: the predicate deciding whether a send-keys payload was actually submitted to the orchestrator pane, as opposed to left composing in the input box.

wrap-boundary collision: the state in which an undelivered payload's cursor geometry is byte-identical to the empty-composer baseline, because the payload wrapped to land the cursor back on the baseline column and row.

prompt-row discriminator: the tie-breaker replacing the tail-matching backstop, resolving an unchanged-geometry reading by testing whether the prompt glyph is anchored at the start of the row the cursor rests on.
residue class: the narrow set of payload shapes for which the primary geometry comparison is provably insufficient and a secondary signal is required.
